answer: **Yes.** The excerpt balances scene and exposition well. The present moment is dramatized in real time: Gregor wakes, sees his body, tries again and again to roll onto his side, touches the itchy spot and looks at the clock. Background is woven into this through his interior monologue rather than delivered in separate blocks. We learn about his job as a traveling salesman, his parents' debt to the boss, his five years of service and his resentment of the boss. Because this exposition comes through his anxious, real-time thoughts, the story keeps moving. The ticking clock and the missed train add tension, so the context never feels dry and the scene never feels static.
